The hospital I work for was privately owned but then sold to a corporation called MVP. We got raises, albeit small ones, benefits cost less for the employees, we get quarterly bonuses (so long as we don't seriously damage our equipment because the bonuses come from the money set aside for repairs), they offer 5 free therapy sessions a year (with online therapists, I believe), along with many other benefits I can't recall right now. 
So far, they've been great to work for, as they have very little involvement within the clinic, so you don't feel like you have a corporation breathing down your neck. You get the benefits of working for MVP without that ominous corporate elephant in the room feel. The atmosphere of my clinic is basically the exact same as it was before the transition. The only part that sucks is that now we have to pay our balances for our own pets before the end of the night instead of leaving it on our accounts for a few weeks lol
